en.title: To God Be the Glory
en.author: Fanny J. Crosby
stanzas:
[G]To God be the glory, great [C]things He hath [G]done,
So loved He the world that He [D7]gave us His [G]Son,
[G]Who yielded His life an a[C]tonement for [G]sin,
[G]And opened the life gate that [D7]all may go [G]in.

Oh, perfect redemption, the purchase of blood,
To every believer the promise of God;
The vilest offender who truly believes,
That moment from Jesus a pardon receives.

Great things He hath taught us, great things He hath done,
And great our rejoicing through Jesus the Son;
But purer, and higher, and greater will be
Our wonder, our transport, when Jesus we see.
en.chorus:
[G]Praise the Lord, [D7]praise the Lord, let the [G]earth hear His voice!
[G]Praise the Lord, [D7]praise the Lord, let the [G]people rejoice!
Oh, [C]come to the Father, through [G]Jesus the Son,
And [G]give Him the glory, great [D7]things He hath [G]done.

notes: Three stanzas and refrain — the whole hymn; Crosby wrote no more. Text from Timeless Truths; hymnary's representative text (Our Great Redeemer's Praise) agrees word-for-word apart from house style: "life-gate" for "life gate", "O perfect redemption" for "Oh, perfect redemption", "ev'ry" for "every", "O come to the Father" for "Oh, come to the Father", and lowercased pronouns. Refrain line division follows this source's four lines; hymnary breaks the first two of them in half again (six refrain lines). Key: A-flat major on both hymnary's tune page and the Timeless Truths score; G and A are each a semitone away and FORMAT.md's preference order picks G, which is the usual guitar key for this hymn anyway. Independently cross-checked 2026-08-01 against the SDA Hymnal (no. 341), which confirms all three of the readings that modernised printings change: "that all may go in", "a pardon receives", and "hath" throughout. Recorded so nobody "corrects" them later: amazinghymns.com prints a modernised text reading "that we may go in", "forgiveness receives" and "has done" — that is a revision, not Crosby's 1875 wording, and is not adopted here.
